raw_text:
Here is a focused 1-week deload that uses the same exercise selection as the prior hypertrophy block, but reduces both volume and intensity to facilitate recovery while preserving technique and neural readiness. It can be dropped in immediately before starting the next block.

Deload Week Overview
- Goals: reduce total weekly training volume and intensity, maintain movement patterns, promote recovery, preserve strength adaptations, and stay mentally engaged.
- Structure: 4 training days (same split as the prior block), with reduced sets and controlled RPEs. Keep tempo slightly conservative to reinforce technique.
- Load guidance: use 60–70% of usual working weights for main lifts. For accessory moves, use 50–60% of usual loads or simply perform with minimal loading while focusing on form.
- Tempo: 2–0–2–0 or 3–0–1–0 (slower eccentrics preferred for technique and tendon health).
- RPE targets: aim for RPE 6–7 on main lifts, RPE 5–6 on accessories.
- Recovery focus: prioritize sleep, nutrition, hydration, and 5–10 minutes of mobility/massage per day.

Weekly Schedule (4 training days)
Note: Keep the same day arrangement as the prior hypertrophy block (e.g., Day 1: Push, Day 2: Pull, Day 3: Legs, Day 4: Upper/Lower or a mirrored split). If you use a full-body or upper-lower split, adapt accordingly but maintain deload principles.

Day 1 – Push (same exercises as prior block)
- Warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio or mobility; warm-up sets for each main movement.
- Main Lift 1: Barbell Bench Press
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 5–6
  - Tempo: 3-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70% of usual working weight
  - RPE target: 6–7
- Main Lift 2: Overhead Press
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 6–8
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE target: 6–7
- Accessory 1: Incline Dumbbell Press
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 8–10
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light–moderate (50–60% usual)
  - RPE target: 5–6
- Accessory 2: Lateral Raises
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 12–15
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
  - RPE target: 5–6
- Triceps Work: Rope Pushdowns
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 12–15
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
  - RPE target: 5–6

Day 2 – Pull
- Warm-up
- Main Lift 1: Barbell Row or Pendlay Row
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 5–6
  - Tempo: 3-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE: 6–7
- Main Lift 2: Pull-Ups or Lat Pulldown
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 6–8
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: bodyweight or light assistance
  - RPE: 6–7
- Accessory 1: Seated Cable Row
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 10–12
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
- Accessory 2: Face Pulls
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 12–15
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
- Biceps: Dumbbell Curls
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 10–12
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light

Day 3 – Legs
- Warm-up
- Main Lift 1: Back Squat or Front Squat
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 5–6
  - Tempo: 3-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE: 6–7
- Main Lift 2: Romanian Deadlift or Leg Curl (Romanian preferred if squat form holds)
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 6–8
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE: 6–7
- Accessory 1: Walking Lunges or Split Squat
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 10–12 per leg
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
- Accessory 2: Leg Extensions
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 12–15
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
- Calves: Standing Calf Raises
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 12–15
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light

Day 4 – Upper/Lower or Pull-Angled Session
- Warm-up
- Main Lift 1: Dumbbell Bench or Incline Barbell
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 5–6
  - Tempo: 3-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE: 6–7
- Main Lift 2: Seated Rows or T-Bar Row
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 6–8
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: 60–70%
  - RPE: 6–7
- Accessory 1: Dumbbell Flyes
  - Sets × Reps: 2 × 10–12
  - Tempo: 2-0-2-0
  - Load: light
- Accessory 2: Core Work
  - Options: Planks, ab wheel, or cable rotations
  - Sets × Reps: 3 × 30–60 seconds planks or 2–3 sets of 12–15 reps
  - Load: bodyweight or light resistance

General deload parameters
- Volume reduction: Roughly 40–60% fewer total sets per week than the peak hypertrophy block. The above plan reduces sets per main lift to 3–3–3–3 across the four days and keeps accessories lighter.
- Intensity reduction: Work sets at 60–70% of usual for main lifts; keep RPE in the 6–7 range.
- Rest intervals: 60–90 seconds between accessory sets; 2–3 minutes between main lifts if needed, but avoid extended rest to keep a light metabolic stimulation.
- Technique focus: Use the deload to refine form, tempo, breathing, and bracing. Consider tempo checks with a coach or video review.

Recovery and nutrition guidance
- Sleep: Target 7–9 hours per night; if fatigue is high, aim for closer to 9.
- Nutrition: Maintain a slight caloric balance or modest surplus if you are in a growth phase, with protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day to maintain lean tissue. Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day water (adjust for sweat loss).
- Recovery tools: 10–15 minutes of light mobility and/or myofascial release daily; consider light SMR on quads, glutes, pecs, and lats.
- Deload monitoring: Keep a short notes log of how you feel (fatigue, soreness, motivation). If you feel unusually fatigued or joints feel off, add an extra rest day or revert to even lighter loads.

Progression to Next Block
- After the deload, re-test or re-evaluate loads for the next hypertrophy-to-strength transition. Start the next block at roughly 2–5% higher than the peak load you used before the deload, but be prepared to regress slightly if fatigue carries over.
- If plan: build into a 3- or 4-week blocks with progressive overload, then a brief higher-intensity block or a tailored deload as needed.

Optional alternatives
- If you prefer a slightly more conventional deload, you can reduce sets per exercise by 2 per main lift and keep the same weights for the first two days, then reduce by 50% on accessory work.
- If using an athlete-administered auto-regulation protocol, you can cap RPE targets at 6–7 and let the athlete choose weights within that range on the fly.
